boundedFindings.priorQuestion: Whether the Department of Corrections investigation and its $100 fee apply to the streamlined route.

statute: RSA 651:5 IX currently says that when a petition is timely brought, the court shall require a Department of Corrections report and the department shall charge $100 unless the petitioner is indigent or the matter is a not-guilty, dismissed or not-prosecuted case under paragraph II.
The current text does not expressly name the post-2018 violation/class-B subparagraphs III(a)(2) and III(b)(2) as an exception.
officialForm: NHJB-3057-DSe page 2 separates violations/class-B misdemeanors from class-A misdemeanors/felonies: the former use the court order on page 3, while the latter are the forms that state a DOC investigation/report is requested.
Page 3 contains the violation/class-B court order and certificate path; it does not contain a DOC-report step.
officialChecklist: The held Judicial Branch checklist states that for a violation or class-B misdemeanor after January 1, 2019, the court reviews the request, may conditionally grant it, sends notice to the prosecutor, and the charge will not be referred to DOC for investigation.
The same checklist distinguishes the additional $100 DOC investigation fee as applying only if the matter requires a DOC referral.

proposedProductRules: For this exact family only, when the target is a post-2018 violation or class-B misdemeanor that has been independently established as the highest offense and otherwise satisfies III/VI, do not route the petition to DOC, do not request the DOC questionnaire, and do not present the DOC $100 investigation fee as a route fee.
Keep the $125 court filing fee per court location. Keep the conditional NHJB-2311 plus NHJB-2328 pair for a participant who cannot pay that court filing fee.

Separate the possible Department of Safety/state-police post-order research-and-correction fee under RSA 651:5 X(d), up to $100, from the DOC investigation fee. For a conviction it is not automatically exempt merely because the route is streamlined; disclose its possible application and the indigency affidavit waiver path through the held waiver form evidence. Do not conflate it with the criminal-history-request fee.
Do not use NH-FEE-WAIVER-2886-WITH-2328-CONFIDENTIAL or any vacated-conviction packet as evidence or a companion for this family.
uncertaintyAndGate: The route-specific form/checklist support no DOC referral, but RSA 651:5 IX remains facially broad. This is a source-supported proposed operational rule with a statutory-text conflict, not an adopted legal resolution.
Keep FEE_AND_WAIVER BLOCKED_LEGAL_INPUT until an owner/counsel-authorized adoption resolves the conflict and the candidate guidance is deliberately updated.

boundedFindings.priorQuestion: What a conditional grant means operationally, what the participant must do, notice timing, and when annulment becomes final.

statute: Under RSA 651:5 III(a)(2) and III(b)(2), after the petition states eligibility, the court submits notice of its determination to the person and prosecutor.
The prosecutor has 20 days from receipt of the notice to object, and only on ineligibility or incomplete sentence terms.
If the prosecutor does not timely object, or the court denies the objection, the court shall annul the conviction.
officialForm: NHJB-3057-DSe page 3 provides the violation/class-B conditional order: the prosecutor receives 20 days from receipt, and if no timely objection is made or the objection is denied, the court issues the Certificate of Annulment.
The form includes a court field for the date sent to the prosecutor, supporting receipt-based tracking without inventing a participant deadline.
officialChecklist: The checklist says the court may issue an order conditionally granting the petition, notice goes to the prosecutor, the 20 days run from the prosecutor's receipt, and the charge is not referred to DOC.
It says that after no objection and a court grant, the certificate of annulment is mailed to the participant.

proposedProductRules: Describe the first court order as conditional/interim; do not represent it as completed annulment or final certificate issuance.

The participant does not serve the prosecutor on this route. The court supplies the notice. Prompt the participant to retain the court notice, ask the clerk for the prosecutor-receipt/date information when needed, and diary the 20-day window from prosecutor receipt.

Do not invent a participant response deadline, a required post-grant filing, a DOC questionnaire, or a hearing. The inspected sources identify no participant action after a conditional grant beyond monitoring the notice/certificate process and responding to any direct court request through appropriate legal help.

Treat a timely prosecutor objection as pending until the court resolves it. Treat no timely objection or a denied objection as the statutory trigger for the court to annul and issue the certificate; only then describe the record as annulled.

Preserve RSA 651:5 IV, VII and VIII: a denial creates a three-year re-petition interval, a new charge that could bar or extend timing holds action until disposition, and a petition failing III-VI is dismissed without a hearing.
uncertaintyAndGate: The form, checklist and statute establish the notice clock and certificate sequence but do not define administrative timing from prosecutor receipt/no objection to certificate mailing or a participant's response mechanics to a prosecutor objection.
Keep ROUTE_OPTIONS BLOCKED_LEGAL_INPUT until this proposed process rule is adopted by the appropriate owner/legal authority; do not claim an automatic completion date.

boundedFindings.priorQuestion: How to classify highest offense when convictions have different disposition dates and how RSA 651:5 VI applies to the whole record.

statute: RSA 651:5 III(a)(2) applies to a post-2018 violation where the violation was the highest offense of conviction; III(b)(2) does the same for a post-2018 class-B misdemeanor.
III(a)(1) and III(b)(1) separately describe the not-highest post-2018 cases, so a target that is not highest does not qualify for this streamlined subparagraph.
The statute does not define highest offense of conviction or specify how to compare offenses whose dispositions/conviction dates differ.
wholeRecord: RSA 651:5 VI(a) bars a petition if annulment of any part of the record is barred under V.
RSA 651:5 VI(b) bars a petition until the time requirements under III and IV for all offenses of record have been met.
RSA 651:5 VII delays action when a new charge could create a V bar or extend the III/IV/VI timing; VIII requires dismissal without hearing when III-VI are not met.

The held checklist instructs that when there is more than one offense stemming from the same arrest, all charge time requirements must be met, subject to its minor-motor-vehicle exception. NHJB-3057-DSe page 2 requires the applicant to certify that the time requirements for all convictions have been met.

proposedProductRules: Do not select the streamlined route from the target charge's date alone. Build a complete record table for every conviction/offense of record with offense level at conviction, conviction/disposition date, sentence-completion date, applicable III period, any V bar, enhanced-penalty/RSA 259:39 status, and pending-charge status.

Require the target's conviction date to be on or after January 1, 2019, the target classification to be violation or class B misdemeanor, and a court-record-supported highest-offense determination before using this family. If the target is not highest, do not call it streamlined; route assessment belongs to the standard conviction family after its own checks.

Do not use the newest or latest disposition date as a proxy for highest offense. Where dispositions have different dates and the court record does not expressly resolve the highest offense, stop for manual court-record/legal review; do not invent a severity ordering or eligibility result.

Apply each offense's own paragraph III/IV timing and then apply the whole-record gate in VI. A qualifying target cannot bypass a different offense's longer waiting period, a V-barred offense, or a pending VII charge. Unknown offense/date/sentence facts remain a stop.

Treat one petition per charge as a filing-form rule, not a waiver of the whole-record gate. Include out-of-state convictions only according to VI-a's New Hampshire-equivalence rule; do not silently decide equivalence.
uncertaintyAndGate: The bounded primary sources clearly establish the whole-record freeze but do not provide a definition or authoritative cross-date ranking for highest offense of conviction.
This remains ROUTE_OPTIONS BLOCKED_LEGAL_INPUT. The proposed record-table/manual-review rule is conservative product handling, not a legal construction or owner adoption.

adoptionRequirementsBeforeAnyReclassific: An authorized owner or counsel-approved legal-design record must adopt or reject the route-specific no-DOC interpretation against the facially broad RSA 651:5 IX text.
The native legal record and participant surfaces must be updated together for DOC/state-police fee distinctions and conditional-grant timing; no packet bytes should be called PASS from this draft.
The highest-offense cross-date rule must be resolved by an authoritative determination or remain a manual legal hold; RSA 651:5 VI whole-record screening must remain enforced.
